analysis.title: Applesauce: Hard to Call it Capitulation When the World's Biggest Stock is at All-Time Highs
key_insights: BTIG's Krinsky calls AAPL extremely vulnerable. It is the best-performing Mag7 stock YTD (+30%, more than 2x the next best) and closed -1.22% below its 52-week high while SPX closed below its 200 DMA.

In the last 20 years AAPL has been closer to a 52-week high on a day SPX closed below its 200 DMA only 14 times. On a 40-day forward basis AAPL was negative in every instance, averaging -15.58%. The 14 days fall in three distinct periods, so the sample is small and statistically insignificant.
Expects AAPL to fall along with SPX as SPX works down toward the 7,000-7,100 target.
Sentiment talk of a 'clearing event' and 'washout' is premature. Capitulation is hard to claim while the largest stock in the world is about 1% below all-time highs.
SPX outcomes after the prior occurrences: the 2007 case started a bear market with SPX falling another 55%. After June 2010 SPX fell another 7.7%. After the first 2011 occurrence SPX fell 11.6%.
Healthcare (XLV) hit a record 19% premium to its 200 DMA and is starting to roll over. Near-term risk is toward $176, with potential toward $165.
Banks (BKX) are trading poorly, have lost the 200 DMA and broke the uptrend from the 2025 lows.
Semis (SOXX) still carry downside risk toward the April breakout point ($120 SOXX, $415 SMH), but are tactically oversold. Guidance is to fade rallies and not press weakness.
Bitcoin is down about 30% in two months and broke through the ~66k risk level, opening the door toward 60k.
Precious metals keep breaking lower. They are tactically oversold with poor sentiment, but BTIG sees gold downside toward about $3,500.
Copper broke down after losing its 200 DMA, and XME is at fresh lows with its 200 DMA turning lower. BTIG sees further downside after tactical bounces.
